resources.string: Demo mode starts a separate simulated session. Export the current session first if you want to keep it.
Start a scan to see nearby Bluetooth advertisers and Wi-Fi networks. Everything stays on this device.
Advertisements can take a moment to appear. Keep the app visible while scanning.
Android requires nearby-device and precise-location access to receive Bluetooth advertisements and Wi-Fi scan results. Location services must be on. Scans stay on your phone.
Scanning needs Nearby devices and Precise location. Enable them in app settings, then start again.
Turn on Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and Location services in Android settings, then start scanning again. Available channels can scan independently.
Signal strength varies with walls, interference, and device orientation. It does not measure distance or direction.
Choose how strong a signal must be to appear. Stronger signals generally favor closer devices; walls and interference affect readings. This sets a signal filter, not a distance in meters.

Applies immediately to Bluetooth LE, Wi-Fi, new alerts, and newly recorded baseline devices. Your choice is saved. Existing observations and past alerts stay in the session report, which marks whether each signal is within the selected range.
Widen the scan range to include weaker signals, or move closer to a device.
Signature matches are estimates based on advertised data. They cannot confirm a device model, owner, or how it is being used.
This supplied signature needs hardware verification. It is shown for review and does not trigger an automatic alert.
New, stronger signals outside your baseline.
New high and medium priority matches appear here once they reach your signal threshold. Unverified signatures stay in Devices.
Alerts use a smoothed signal of at least %1$d dBm. A match is a prompt to review, not proof of a device type.
Set a baseline. Notice what changes.
Record your surroundings before monitoring. Baseline devices stay visible and do not trigger new-device alerts.
All signals seen now are being added. Tap Finish when you have captured your surroundings.
Start scanning before recording a baseline.
Stronger signals are more likely to be nearby. This setting does not establish a room boundary.
One short tone for each new qualifying device.
Export all observations, including expired or out-of-range signals, as a CSV file. Each row marks whether it is within the selected scan range. Demo reports are labeled DEMO.
Could not save the report. Choose another location and try again.
Scan for devices before exporting a report.
Clear this session and its baseline? Export a CSV first if you want to keep the observations.
No account. No cloud. No Internet permission. Sessions remain in memory until reset or the app process closes; export a report to keep them.

BLE advertisers and Wi-Fi access points, hotspots, and advertised Wi-Fi Direct networks. Silent devices and devices connected as Wi-Fi clients may not appear. Wi-Fi requests run every 35 seconds and Android may delay them. Scanning pauses when the app leaves the foreground.
Waiting for enough fresh readings to compare.
Move a few steps, then pause to compare. Watch whether the received signal gets stronger or weaker.
The selected address is no longer sending fresh observations. Move around slowly and wait for the signal to return.
Resume scanning to receive new readings. Finding also pauses when you leave this app.
Enable this device’s Bluetooth or Wi-Fi channel and Location services, then pause and resume scanning. The other radio cannot replace this signal.
Below your scan-range filter. This selected device is still followed here.
Wi-Fi readings usually update no faster than the 35-second scan cycle, and Android may delay them. Pause after moving and wait for a fresh reading.

This compares signal strength, not direction or distance. Walls, interference, and device orientation can change readings. The selected address is followed even outside your scan range; if the device changes its address, select its new entry.
